evidence.snippet: We present a family with myopathy with early onset proximal muscle weakness, facial muscle involvement and ophthalmoplegia.

nodes.description: Founding dominant motor-domain variant (E706K) in the SH1 helix, from the original Swedish family.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant myopathy: missense mutation (Glu-706 --> Lys) in the myosin heavy chain IIa gene.
evidence.snippet: We identified a missense mutation, Glu-706 --> Lys, which is located in a highly conserved region of the motor domain, the so-called SH1 helix region.

nodes.description: Dominant splice-donor variant causing in-frame skipping of exon 39 and loss of residues 1860-1891 of the distal tail.

evidence.reference_title: Dominantly inherited myosin IIa myopathy caused by aberrant splicing of MYH2.
evidence.snippet: Whole-genome sequencing identified a heterozygous MYH2 variant, segregating with the disease in the three affected individuals: c.5673 + 1G > C.

evidence.reference_title: MYH2-associated myopathy caused by a novel splice-site variant.
evidence.snippet: A novel variant, MYH2 c.5673+1G>C, was detected in the proband and subsequently found to segregate with disease in five additional family members.
